title: Night in the Woods: graphic gaze and restrained mouths

people.name: Scott Benson
people.role: Art and animation; co-designer and art director

people.name: Charles Huettner
people.role: Additional animation, described by Benson as animation work on the game

summary: Large, high-contrast eye shapes make attention readable while mouths occupy very little of the face.

observations.text: In the publisher's Miller's storefront still, the two profile characters each have one dominant elongated eye; Mae's paired orange eyes stand out against her dark face. Tiny mouth marks leave the eyes as the main facial signal.
Benson describes the intended setting as a close group of chatty friends in a bustling small town and explicitly identifies his own art and animation work and Huettner's animation contribution.

mistIdeas: Our inference: let gaze establish the target before changing MIST's mouth, and hold the target until a meaningful event interrupts it.
Our inference: try a small set of strong upper-lid silhouettes, with a tiny neutral mouth. Test whether attention remains readable at the actual display size.
Our inference: reserve asymmetry for suspicion or uncertainty rather than continuously varying both eyes.

title: ANTONBLAST: Anton's open-mouth to clenched-teeth reaction

people.name: Juniper / PinPan
people.role: Lead gameplay animator on AntonBlast, self-credited on artist profile

summary: An official eight-second close-up shows how mouth area and silhouette can dominate a reaction without requiring detailed facial anatomy.

observations.text: At the inspected start of the official clip, Anton has a tall open mouth, separated upper and lower tooth bands and raised arms. At the inspected end, the mouth becomes a large clenched white tooth mass, with narrow eyes and a raised fist. These are sharply different readable shapes.
The dark hair and beard create an angular outline around the bright mouth. The face is not limited to moving small features inside an unchanged oval.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give surprise and determined recovery genuinely different mouth silhouettes instead of scaling one mouth path.
Our inference: test a compressed anticipatory eye pose, a single large reaction peak, and a smaller settled expression. This proposed sequence is a MIST experiment, not measured ANTONBLAST timing.
Our inference: keep MIST's outer housing stable while allowing its digital eye and mouth graphics to deform strongly inside it. Copy the contrast of shapes, not Anton's teeth, beard or colour scheme.

title: Moss - Quill acknowledges the player
summary: A face becomes a relationship when its look and gestures answer the person in front of it.

observations.text: Lico describes deliberate eye contact, returning the player's wave, petting and high-five interactions as ways to build mutual acknowledgement and trust.
He requires personality to survive gameplay actions while input stays immediate and movement fluid; he explicitly seeks nuanced, honest gestures.
The GDC slides identify a reaction system, limited gameplay interruptions using idle cycles, and particle physics to help overlapping action.

mistIdeas: Our inference: give MIST a listening look that locks onto the user before a reply, then a small acknowledgement after understanding.
Our inference: prioritize an incoming user event over decorative idle motion, preserving the current facial pose into the response.
Our inference: let a secondary antenna or chassis settle finish after the principal eye reaction; never require that settle before accepting another event.

title: Cuphead: Pip and Dot: conflicting faces on one body

people.name: Tina Nawrocki
people.role: Animator and designer of this character, identified in her own production post

summary: Two faces share a rectangular body but carry different attitudes.

observations.text: In the idle drawing, the upper face bares clenched teeth while the lower face grins. Their sideways pupils establish attitude inside a stable rectangular silhouette.
The hat drawings contrast lowered lids with sharply angled brows and broader grins. The hat and bow distinguish the two faces.
The mouth-attack drawing separates the domino halves and exposes large teeth while the small faces remain legible.

mistIdeas: Our inference: try an asymmetric MIST listening pose with one lid lower and a restrained mouth.
Our inference: fix two or three identity anchors while the lids and mouth carry a reaction.

title: Wandersong: make the face follow an action

people.name: Greg Lobanov
people.role: Creator; creator/director in his development interview

summary: The bard's singing pose is a useful reference for giving a minimal face one clear job tied to the player's action.

observations.text: A sampled frame of the official first GIF shows the bard with closed eyes and an open mouth inside the colored singing wheel. The face agrees with the action displayed by the surrounding interface.
The official game description says different things respond differently to singing and advertises a dance button usable anywhere.
Lobanov describes a visual style deliberately easy to create new assets for, with individual screens drawn for emotional variation. He calls its rough, playful character an invitation to try things.

mistIdeas: Our inference: choose the mouth from a meaningful state such as speaking, listening, or acknowledging, then let eye shape support that action.
Our inference: use a closed-eye smile only for a completed acknowledgement or delight beat, and return to an attentive gaze afterward.
Our inference: test distinct event poses before adding interpolation. A readable pose should survive as a still at robot-screen scale.
